name: d10SRD

source.commit_subject: feat: publish the audience-facing SRD reference
source.working_tree: clean at the time of vendoring

why_vendored: The rules are an external authority that this product must conform to, and a conformance test that cannot execute the rules is not a conformance test. Transcribing the numbers into a test made the assertion self-referential: it would keep passing while the published rules moved underneath it. The rules module is distributed here so the test executes the real implementation, and the digests below make a divergence from upstream a build failure rather than a silent drift.

files.role: executable rules: abilityModifier, scaleD20DC, resolveCheck, rollCheck
canonicalisation and deterministic d10 derivation; required by d10.mjs
the published document, including the Conformance section and the authority boundary

update_procedure: When upstream d10SRD publishes a change: re-copy the files, update every sha256 and the commit here, bump `version` if upstream did, re-pin game/data/d10srd_conformance.json to the same version, and re-run `npm test`. tests/d10srd-conformance.test.mjs fails until the digests and the two version fields agree, so a partial update cannot pass.
